key_insight: For quantitative questions in perovskite photovoltaics, read-only SQL access to structured device data lifts language-model accuracy to about 51%, versus 16–23% for standard passage retrieval.
engineering_relevance: Materials literature assistants need structured experimental databases—not just searchable text—to reliably compare device performance and summarize measurements across papers.
method: Compute 755 ground-truth answers directly from measured device records.
Benchmark six retrieval architectures over 158,274 passages from 25,662 papers.
Equip an open 14B model with read-only SQL access on a single 24 GB GPU.
evidence_signal: Evaluation uses 45,441 device records: 40,889 human-curated records through 2021 and 4,552 extracted from 2022–2026 literature; SQL-enabled accuracy reaches 51.5% on historical and 50.8% on prospective literature.
watch_item: Accuracy remains near 51%, and deployment depends on accurate extraction and consistent normalization of experimental device records.
paper_title: Benchmark for Structured Retrieval-Augmented Generation in Perovskite Photovoltaics
